Historical Particle Universe SDK headers

These licensed historical headers describe the native Runic Particle Universe ABI. Library implementations, constructors and destructors remain native; this dependency adds no recovered game-function or PU-implementation credit. The original copyright and license statements are retained. upstream-inventory.json pins the unmodified upstream bytes, revision and source paths. OgreCompiler2Pass.h comes from official OGRE v1-6-0 because the historical tokenizer requires that removed API.

HistoricalPuRunic.patch reproduces every change from upstream/ to include/, including dependent-typename and initializer syntax fixes for GCC 4.4.7. The native extensions preserve the original bases and owning containers. Actual GCC 4.4.7 layout probes and native constructor/destructor comparisons establish Manager 0x548, Particle 0xf0, System 0x2f0, Technique 0x5b8, Renderer 0x88, BillboardRenderer 0xa8, RibbonTrailRenderer 0x138, Emitter 0x260 and Affector 0x158. The two renderer plugin headers have their own pinned raw inventory entries.

The DynamicAttribute declarations use the native getValue(Particle*,float) signature. decomp/include/ParticleDynamicAttribute.h includes this single SDK definition. Fixed, Random, Curved and Oscillate native owners, selected virtual slots, layouts and both include orders have comparative coverage. Technique extensions use real owning strings and retain the separately observed neutral byte at 0x5b1; it is distinct from mKeepLocal. Native PointEmitter, BillboardRenderer, RibbonTrailRenderer and LinearForceAffector owners and selected add/remove APIs also have comparative coverage.

Manager efd970 C1 and efd010 D1 establish its owning layout. ef8100 identifies the VisualParticle* pool at 0x510; native game/UI consumers establish time scale, camera, statistics and the paused flag at 0x540. The vector at 0x528 has no discovered element consumer: std::vector<void*> preserves only its owning storage ABI and permits no new element operation. Counter 0x500 and bool 0x540 remain uninitialized by the native constructor, and neutral names do not claim unknown semantics.

These checks cover the declarations and entry points used by recovered game code. They do not certify every historical SDK virtual slot or inline implementation, GPU rendering or a playable hybrid. Pointer-only dependencies in Manager/IToken use forward declarations to avoid unnecessary header coupling.
